data.title: Prioritization
body: # Prioritization
> **Superseded 2026-09-16 by [strategy.md](DOC-35).** Kept as history; where the two disagree, strategy.md wins.
- **Date:** 2026-09-08 (revision of the table from 2026-09-02)
- **Context:** pre-PMF · solo developer · **zero usage data** · `kadence@0.2.1` published
- **Language:** the document stays in Ukrainian until the general migration of `docs/` to English (decision 2026-09-07)
## Why Value/Effort, and why we are not changing it

RICE requires Reach — the number of users a feature will touch. We have zero users, so any number there would be invented, and dividing by an invented number gives a precision that does not exist. For pre-PMF with a solo developer, only the lightest frameworks are usable: **Value/Effort**, with the honest admission that Value is an estimate, not a measurement.
**Value** here does not mean "usefulness in general" but the contribution to a single goal: **get the first users and check whether anyone needs the differentiator.**

Nothing that determines the choice of framework has changed since: not the stage, not the team size, not the availability of usage data. So the framework stays the same. Changing the framework every quarter is a known mistake of its own: the time goes into relearning instead of into decisions, and the estimates stop being comparable between revisions.

**Estimates are input, not an automaton.** The difference between Value 3 and Value 4 does not exist as a fact; it exists as a reason to talk. Where the table contradicts the obvious, the obvious wins — but then the table has to be corrected, not silently ignored.
## Shipped
| Feature | Value | Effort | Where |
| Event journal + folding into state (the core) | 5 | 4 | v0.1 |
| `task add / list / move` | 5 | 2 | v0.1 |
| Conflict-free merge | 5 | 1 | v0.1 — falls out of the core for free |
| Notice about conflict-free merging | 4 | 1 | v0.1 — otherwise the main property is invisible |
| `--json` + `.kadence/README.md` | 4 | 2 | v0.1 |
| Sprint + `sprint close` with velocity | 4 | 3 | v0.1 — the second differentiator |
| Estimate in `task add` | 4 | 1 | v0.1 |
| Static board `kadence board` | 4 | 2 | v0.1 |
| Interactive TUI | 4 | 5 | **0.1.x** — the plan said v0.2 |
| `kadence log` | 3 | 1 | **0.1.x** — the plan said v0.2 |
| estimate-vs-actual | 3 | 3 | **0.1.x** — the plan said v0.2; `sprint close` prints hours per point |
| **Entry point in `CLAUDE.md`** | **5** | **1** | **0.2.1** — was not in the plan |
| **`kadence schema --json`** | 4 | 2 | **0.2.1** — was not in the plan |
| **Error codes + `allowed` in `--json`** | 4 | 2 | **0.2.1** — was not in the plan |
| **`--fields`** | 3 | 1 | **0.2.1** — was not in the plan |
## Not shipped
| Feature | Value | Effort | Decision |

| **`kadence decision`** — "why" as a separate event type | 3 | 2 | v0.3, **gate: Probe B**. The cleanest embodiment of the bet on shared context — and therefore the most dependent on whether the bet is true. If it is, this may turn out to be the product's most important feature; if not, a feature for nobody |
| `context --branch` — context for the whole branch | 3 | 2 | v0.2. `context <task>` removed 2026-09-07: `task show --json` already returns the task's whole history in 948 bytes ([Probe C](DOC-57)) |

| Optional MCP package | **2** ↓ from 3 | 4 | v0.3. [Probe C](DOC-57) measured that a wrapper would have saved ~700 tokens per session against the CLI — the economy argument we leaned on fell away, and no new one appeared. The trigger is a user who **cannot** work in a CLI |
| Import from Backlog.md | 3 | 3 | v0.3 — valuable only if a probe confirms the channel |
| Web UI | 2 | 5 | No |
| Sync with GitHub Issues | 2 | 5 | No — the most frequent request there will be, and the fastest way to become a mediocre bridge instead of a tool in its own right |
| Manual time tracking | 2 | 3 | No — velocity is counted from events, a manual timer contradicts the idea |
| `llms.txt` | 1 | 1 | No — 10% of domains, zero correlation with citations, Google says it does not use it ([research](DOC-38) §6) |
## What the table showed about itself

The four most valuable things shipped in 0.2.1 **were absent from the table**. They came not from planning but from [research into how agents read a repository](DOC-38). One of them — the entry point in `CLAUDE.md` — has Value 5 at Effort 1, the best ratio in the whole document. No prioritization session found it, because it is impossible to order an item that is not on the list.
Plus three items that stood as "v0.2" shipped back in the 0.1 line — the ordering did not survive contact with the work either.

The conclusion is not "planning is not worth it". It is that **for a pre-PMF product, research supplies backlog items more cheaply than prioritization orders them**: prioritization sorts what has already come to mind, and research adds what did not.
## What changed after the probes
The previous version of this document ended with a condition: "the table is valid if a probe confirms the pain".

[Probe A](DOC-55) has been run. The answer is in the middle: conflicts in tasks are real but rare — 15% of repositories, roughly one merge in two hundred, and 89% of them exactly the type our architecture eliminates. So conflict-freedom stayed in the product as **proof**, not as the headline, and the Value column needed no recalculation.

[Probe C](DOC-57) added two numbers and took away one argument: an answer to an agent costs 948 bytes regardless of project size — the advantage is real and now under a guardrail test; and an MCP wrapper would have saved ~700 tokens per session — an advantage we credited ourselves with does not exist.
## The condition under which this table is valid
The same as in September, and it is still unmet: **[Probe B](DOC-49) — 5–7 conversations, the script is ready, not run.**

Every row in "Not shipped" is ordered on the assumption that teams lose context between sessions enough to pay attention for it. Nobody has tested that assumption. `kadence decision` is the starkest example: it is on the list because it follows logically from the bet, not because anyone asked.
Until Probe B is run, the order in this table is an order of guesses. It is better than random and worse than one phone call.
